trig

suite examplestrigsimplipy

Trigonometric identities (demo)

A small public demo suite: Pythagorean and double-angle identities, inverse functions composed with their functions (true only on the principal range), and periodicity. Official vocabulary only.

licence CC0-1.0

Categories
identities
Algebraic trigonometric identities over the reals or complexes, and where they fail (sqrt of a square).
inverse
asin(sin x) = x and friends: true exactly on the principal range of the inverse.
periodicity
Shifts by multiples of pi: periods, half-periods, and where a shifted value coincides.

official cases as LaTeX (.tex)

Solved vs time
time per solved case all suites

y: cases solved (true and false cases answered correctly: the table's solved row). x: wall-clock time per solved case, its median or mean, log scale; only solved cases are timed (a timeout or no verdict is never a fast answer), so a system that solves only easy cases can look fast. Dotted: the Pareto frontier, the routines no other one beats on both (as fast or faster and solving as many or more). Hollow marks: routines with wrong answers; the site ranks any wrong answer below every wrong-free system, so the frontier leaves them out unless asked. A colour and a marker shape per group, its routines joined by a thin line. Whiskers (median view): the 95% interval of the median over the timed cases (distribution-free, from the cases' order statistics): how far the median could move with other cases of the same kind and each one's timing noise; it does not cover a slower or faster run of the whole machine.

The Pi also serves websites, and other work may share core 3 unless it is reserved for the runs (pi5-deploy INSTALL.md, step 15). Clock frequency and temperature are not controlled).

Each cell shows what the system said, coloured by outcome: true ✓ solved, true ✗ wrong, no verdict: the system ran but did not commit to true or false (null); no verdict ✓ (grey ✓, on a contingent case) declined correctly: Correct: neither true nor false holds here. Not counted as solved, since a system that never answers would get this too.

Times: wall-clock seconds per query as the runner measured them (each query in its own forked process; setup and warm-up not timed); totals and medians are over the solved cases only, so a timeout, error or no verdict never counts as a fast answer. Machines: pi5 (indicative): it has some other load: times are a fair guide, large differences between its runs mean something, small ones may be noise (Raspberry Pi 5, 4 cores. Benchmark runs go one at a time, in a low-priority systemd unit (CPUWeight=20, Nice=10); since 2026-10-17, each eval is pinned to core 3 (earlier runs were not pinned). The Pi also serves websites, and other work may share core 3 unless it is reserved for the runs (pi5-deploy INSTALL.md, step 15). Clock frequency and temperature are not controlled).
